html:
A railway built by the British from 1896 to 1901 from the port of Mombasa to Kisumu on Lake Victoria, about 900 kilometres inland. Despite its name, it ran entirely through what is now Kenya; its purpose was to reach Uganda by the lake.

Critics in Parliament mocked it as the "Lunatic Express" for its cost. Most of the labour came from British India: tens of thousands of indentured workers, and about 2,500 died building it. In 1898 two lions at Tsavo killed many workers, the Tsavo man-eaters.

The line shaped modern Kenya:

  • Nairobi grew from a railway depot founded in 1899 and became the capital.
  • The highlands along the line were opened to white settler farms.
  • Many Indian workers and traders stayed, founding Kenya's Asian community.

It was replaced in 2017 by the new Mombasa to Nairobi railway.
sum: A railway built by the British from 1896 to 1901 from the port of Mombasa to Kisumu on Lake Victoria, about 900 kilometres inland. Despite its name, it ran entirely through what is now Kenya; its purpose was to reach Uganda by the lake.
